mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the chromosome sets was most worthwhile: the picture and prose distinguish sister-chromatid separation from division of the shared cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making membrane vesicles was a thin intermediate on its own; its contribution became clear only when they fused with the cell surface.

surprise.text: The copied-genome result emphasized that replication includes noncoding DNA, unlike making a protein.

arbitrary.text: Combining the enlarged cell body with separated chromosome sets felt somewhat like joining two views of the same cell rather than performing a physical action, although the resulting daughter nuclei had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue: the sequence made growth, chromosome separation and division distinct, and the final descendant branches suggest a next question about specialization.
